title: Pack A Section E Inventory — Clone Group Analysis
methodology: READ-ONLY. PowerShell Select-String + regex block extraction for QuestionID, question_state, Topic, Stem, CorrectChoice, DifficultyScore, CognitiveLevel. Stem comparison for clone group identification. All counts verified against S803 baseline.
p1_e_056_status: Certified — S803 restoration confirmed (was Archived in S802, now Certified)

certified_clones.risk: HIGH — 9 Certified items (15.3% of Section E learner pool) deliver near-identical content differentiated only by fictional company name. 3 of 5 clone groups (G1, G3) have 3 Certified members each, meaning the same stem could appear up to 3 times in a single practice session. G3 is particularly risky: P1-E-048 and P1-E-056 share the same CorrectChoice (D), creating a direct duplicate experience.

s804_recommendation.action: Archival candidate assessment for the 9 Certified clone items
s804_recommendation.rationale: 9 Certified items deliver near-identical educational content. For each clone group, archiving N-1 members and retaining 1 seed reduces redundancy while preserving topic coverage.

per_group_recommendation.G1_AP_Duplicate: Retain 1 seed (P1-E-037 recommended as first instance). Archive P1-E-045 and P1-E-053. 3 Certified → 1 Certified, -2 Certified.

s804_recommendation.net_impact: Archiving 4 items reduces Section E Certified from 59 to 55. Pack A total Certified would drop from 482 to 478. This is a defensible quality improvement, not a regression — the archived items add zero unique educational value.
